prayer.text: Saint Raymond of Penyafort, pray for us.

cues.text: A Scholar of Law
Born around 1175 near Barcelona , Raymond displayed exceptional intellectual gifts from a young age, teaching philosophy by twenty.
He eventually earned doctorates in both civil and canon law at the renowned University of Bologna .
There, he taught for several years and published a treatise on ecclesiastical legislation still preserved in the Vatican Library.
Joining the Dominicans

Recalled to Barcelona to serve as archdeacon and vicar general to the local bishop, Raymond was drawn instead to the new mendicant movement, entering the Dominican Order around 1222 after hearing the preaching of Blessed Reginald of Orléans.
In Barcelona, Raymond was associated by tradition with St. Peter Nolasco in the founding of the Mercedarian Order, which was dedicated to ransoming Christian captives held by Muslim powers.
Codifying Canon Law

Summoned to Rome by Pope Gregory IX , Raymond was given the enormous task of gathering and organizing the Church's scattered legal decrees, unsystematized for the previous eighty years, into a single authoritative collection.
The resulting five books of Decretals , completed in 1234, were declared by Gregory the sole authoritative text for canon law study at Paris and Bologna.
They remained foundational to Church law for nearly seven centuries, until the 1917 Code of Canon Law.
Declining the Miter
Gregory IX was so pleased with Raymond's work that he appointed him Archbishop of Tarragona.
Raymond declined the honor, preferring to remain a humble friar.
In his biographers' account, providence intervened further when a sudden illness helped persuade the pope to release him from the appointment altogether.
Master General of the Dominicans
Elected Master General of the Dominican Order in 1238, Raymond revised the order's constitutions during his brief two-year tenure before resigning to return to more direct pastoral work.
According to a traditional account, Raymond encouraged St. Thomas Aquinas to compose the Summa contra Gentiles, which has sometimes been associated with missionary efforts among Muslims and Jews.
Legacy
Raymond lived, by tradition, to nearly a hundred years old, dying at Barcelona on January 6, 1275, and was canonized by Pope Clement VIII in 1601.
His Summa de Poenitentia et Matrimonio is considered one of the first true manuals of moral theology for confessors.
He remains honored today as the patron saint of canon lawyers, a scholar whose careful, systematic work helped organize the medieval Church's developing body of canon law.
